title: Upper zone temperature sensor fault
shortDescription: Upper zone thermistor reads out of range.
fullDescription: Whirlpool dual-zone wine coolers display E1 when the upper zone temperature sensor reports an open or shorted reading. The unit defaults to a fail-safe set point until the sensor is replaced.
symptoms: Upper zone runs warm or cold

fixSteps.title: Unplug
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the cooler from power for 15 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the upper liner cover and reseat the thermistor connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the thermistor if the resistance is far from spec.

whenToCallPro: Call if you cannot access the rear of the liner.

faq.a: Use the fail-safe temperature for a few days at most.

title: Lower zone temperature sensor fault
shortDescription: Lower zone thermistor reads out of range.
fullDescription: E2 indicates the lower zone sensor is open or shorted. The unit holds a fail-safe set point until the sensor is replaced.

fixSteps.title: Reseat sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the lower liner cover and reseat the connector.

whenToCallPro: Call if liner access is unsafe.

faq.a: Yes for a short period at the fail-safe temp.

title: Evaporator sensor fault
shortDescription: Evaporator coil sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription: E3 indicates the evaporator temperature sensor is reporting an out-of-range value, which prevents proper defrost cycling.

fixSteps.title: Access coil
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the rear interior panel to access the evaporator.

whenToCallPro: Many owners prefer a tech for evaporator work.

faq.a: Defrost cannot trigger without a valid sensor reading.

title: Door open too long
shortDescription: Door has been open beyond the alarm threshold.
fullDescription: E4 alerts the user that a door has remained open for several minutes. Verify the door reed switch is being triggered by the magnet.

fixSteps.title: Close door
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the door fully latches and the gasket seals.

fixSteps.title: Check magnet
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the door magnet aligned with the reed switch.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the reed switch if door is closed but E4 stays.

faq.q: Why does it trip when door is closed?
faq.a: Likely the magnet is shifted or the reed switch failed.

title: Compressor fan fault
shortDescription: Condenser fan does not report speed.
fullDescription: E5 indicates the compressor compartment fan is not running at expected speed. Dust, a loose plug, or worn motor are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum coils
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum the rear or bottom condenser coils and fan.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the condenser fan if it does not spin freely.

whenToCallPro: Call if the unit is built into cabinetry.

faq.a: No, the compressor will overheat without airflow.

title: Compressor over-current
fullDescription: E6 trips when the compressor draws more current than allowed. Restricted airflow, a failing start relay, or a worn compressor are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Replace start relay
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the compressor start relay if E6 returns.

fixSteps.title: Service compressor
fixSteps.instruction: If E6 persists, the compressor needs evaluation.

faq.a: Every six months in dusty homes.

title: Cabinet too warm
shortDescription: Internal temperature is above set point for extended time.
fullDescription: HI indicates the cabinet has been warmer than set point for over an hour. Causes include overloading, ambient too hot, blocked airflow, or sealed-system loss.

fixSteps.title: Reduce load
fixSteps.instruction: Remove some bottles to allow airflow between them.

fixSteps.title: Check vents
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm front and back grilles are clear.

fixSteps.title: Service refrigerant
fixSteps.instruction: If HI persists with normal load and ambient, call a sealed-system tech.

faq.a: Brief warm spells are tolerable; sustained heat will cook wine.

title: Cabinet too cold
shortDescription: Internal temperature is below set point.
fullDescription: LO indicates the cabinet temperature is several degrees below the set point for an extended period. A stuck damper, failed fan, or thermistor drift are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Check damper
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the inter-zone damper opens and closes freely.

fixSteps.title: Verify thermistors
fixSteps.instruction: Test thermistor resistance against spec at room temp.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: If sensors are good, replace the control board.

whenToCallPro: Call if you cannot rule out the sensor or damper.
videoSearchQuery: Whirlpool wine cooler LO too cold

faq.a: Yes, cork shrinks and lets air in.

title: Defrost active or stuck
fullDescription: dF indicates the cooler is running its defrost cycle. If dF stays for over an hour, the defrost heater or thermostat is likely failed.

fixSteps.title: Wait
fixSteps.instruction: A normal defrost completes in 15-30 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Inspect heater
fixSteps.instruction: If dF persists, test defrost heater continuity.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: Replace defrost thermostat if shorted closed.

whenToCallPro: Call if you cannot reach the evaporator safely.

faq.a: About every 12-24 hours of compressor run time.

title: Power outage detected
shortDescription: Cooler logged a recent power loss.
fullDescription: PO indicates the cooler lost power and the cabinet may have warmed during the outage. Pressing any key clears the alert.

fixSteps.title: Check breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the breaker did not trip from a surge.

videoSearchQuery: Whirlpool wine cooler PO power outage

faq.a: Brief outages rarely affect wine; long outages may.
